editorial:
Imagine being a quiet housewife who always does what she is told, only to suddenly find yourself running a whole factory. That is exactly what happens to Suzanne in this funny story set in 1970s France. Her husband, Robert, is a mean boss who cares more about money than people. When he has a heart attack because his workers are striking, Suzanne steps in to help. You will love watching her go from a shy wife to a confident leader who actually cares about her employees. The vibe is light and breezy, making it a great pick for a relaxed movie night.

The acting is top-notch, especially seeing Suzanne find her voice while her husband recovers. The pacing is quick and keeps you interested without feeling rushed. While some of the plot points are a bit predictable, the charm of the characters makes up for it. If you enjoy stories about people finding their power, you should definitely give this a try. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for a crisp look, or you might want to rent it on Apple TV if you prefer. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great move if you love collecting high-quality films.
endingExplained: In the end, Suzanne fully embraces her new role as a leader. She stops being the quiet trophy wife and starts making her own decisions. Robert eventually recovers, but he realizes he cannot just go back to being a bully because Suzanne has changed the dynamic of the factory. They find a new balance in their marriage where Suzanne has more respect and power, showing that she is much more than just a pretty face.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about underdogs finding their strength.
